Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across business and general-news outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by the Jensen Huang/Nvidia saga - his shock reinstatement as CEO after Trump administration pressure, the market whiplash that followed, and the political and governance fallout. Secondary threads include corporate earnings (Best Buy, American Airlines), scrutiny of prediction markets, and lingering Middle East shipping/oil risks.

stories.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump pressure campaign
stories.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reversed itself just days after saying it would not bring Huang back, reinstating him as president, CEO and director and saying it had received input from senior U.S. officials that his return poses no national security risk. Axios reported that Trump personally called into the board meeting to push for Huang's return, while Forbes noted Huang disclosed additional undisclosed affairs to the board before the vote.

stories.headline: Tech stocks slide as Huang-fueled rally fades and trade fears resurface
stories.summary: After Nvidia's reinstatement news sparked a rally that added nearly $1 trillion in market value, shares pulled back the next day as Anthropic dropped below its IPO price and investor relief subsided. Bloomberg and WSJ both described a market swinging wildly on AI sentiment, with fresh tariff fears also weighing on sentiment.

stories.headline: Trump's Nvidia intervention triggers bipartisan political backlash
stories.summary: Republican lawmakers in Washington are reportedly dismayed by Trump's direct involvement in restoring Huang, even as it delighted Wall Street and Silicon Valley; Politico separately reports that 2028 Democratic hopefuls are framing the episode as evidence of government corruption. Governance experts quoted by Axios said the board's reversal showed a "lack of backbone" and left Huang effectively unaccountable.

stories.headline: American Airlines falls further behind Delta and United
stories.summary: Despite flying more passengers than any other U.S. carrier, American Airlines is losing money while rivals Delta and United post billions in profits, weighed down by debt and fuel costs.

stories.headline: NYC Council presses Kalshi and Polymarket over marketing to young users
stories.summary: New York City Council members called on executives from the leading prediction-market platforms to testify as lawmakers investigate whether the firms used deceptive tactics to attract younger users; NYT reported the probe found 18- to 20-year-olds in the city are losing money at a high rate.

stories.headline: Best Buy posts its strongest comparable sales growth in five years
stories.summary: Best Buy beat quarterly expectations and raised its full-year guidance after posting comparable sales growth of 6.1%, its best performance in five years.

stories.headline: Oil prices rebound as Middle East shipping risks persist
stories.summary: Oil prices recovered from early losses as traders balanced continuing threats to energy shipments in the Middle East against expectations of a global supply surplus; a related WSJ report said U.S. officials are investigating Iran as a possible culprit behind dozens of new cyberattacks on ships.

stories.headline: Disney leans into streaming expansion without clarifying the cost
stories.summary: Disney is adding more content, sports programming and possibly a free tier in a bid to turn streaming into a growth engine, though the company has been vague about the associated costs.

Business.gaps: Puck had no recent business coverage found in search or feeds; Business Insider had no feed items provided and blocks search, so nothing could be reported for it.

US politics.overview: Coverage across US politics outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang at Trump's urging, which has triggered bipartisan congressional anger, national-security questions, and investigations plans once Democrats take control in January. A second major thread is the resignation of Rep. Jimmy Gomez after a damning House Ethics sexual misconduct finding, layered atop a rising-odds government shutdown fight and other Capitol Hill mechanics stories.

stories.headline: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang sparks bipartisan Capitol Hill backlash
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump's urging, and lawmakers in both parties are demanding answers, with Democrats like Hakeem Jeffries vowing a 'swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance' once they take power in January, while Republicans like Sen. John Curtis say 'I have some questions' about what changed since the board's prior stance.

stories.headline: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after Ethics Committee finds 'substantial evidence' of sexual misconduct
stories.summary: The House Ethics Committee found Gomez engaged in sexual misconduct with a staffer that 'could constitute criminal misdemeanor sexual abuse,' prompting the California Democrat, who had already lost re-election, to announce he will resign effective Dec. 1 despite disputing the report's conclusions.

stories.headline: Shutdown odds rise as GOP leaders weigh cutting off Iran war funding
stories.summary: With a Dec. 11 shutdown deadline looming, key Senate Republicans are signaling openness to Democrats' demand to fund the Pentagon while cutting off funding for the unpopular Iran conflict.

stories.headline: Appeals court rules lack of quorum invalidated House proxy voting
stories.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that pandemic-era House proxy votes were unconstitutional because the chamber lacked the quorum required by the Constitution to conduct business, a decision with potentially sweeping implications for past legislation.

stories.headline: New records show DOJ and judge clashed over scope of Ilhan Omar search warrant
stories.summary: Newly unsealed, heavily redacted records show a federal judge raising Speech or Debate Clause concerns with DOJ officials before the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's home, with the evidence sought reportedly spanning decades.

stories.headline: Rand Paul draft group forms to back a 2028 presidential run
stories.summary: A new group is working to persuade Sen. Rand Paul to seek the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, an early move in the party's post-midterm jockeying.

stories.headline: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
stories.summary: House Democratic investigators, led in part by Rep. Jamie Raskin, are examining whether companies tied to Donald Trump Jr.'s investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited from government access since his father's reelection.

stories.headline: Supreme Court's Second Amendment case thrown into disarray by last-minute shuffle
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports a late surprise has reshuffled a pending Second Amendment case before the Supreme Court, with a companion piece examining the justices' use of dicta in gun-rights rulings.

US politics.gaps: No recent (last 24-48h) items could be found from NOTUS or Cook Political Report; their most relevant available content was weeks to months old. Politico, NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian coverage reflected only the feed items provided, since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is overwhelmingly dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO just days after resigning in an affairs scandal, with outlets scrutinizing the political pressure campaign behind it, a related export-control blacklisting, and a sharp reversal in AI stocks. Beyond the Nvidia drama, outlets are tracking new agentic AI tools from Anthropic, internal safety debates at frontier labs, data center energy strategy, and a major cybersecurity acquisition.

stories.headline: AI stocks give back gains as Nvidia and Anthropic rally fades
stories.summary: Nvidia, AMD, Micron, Arm and Marvell all fell sharply a day after posting huge gains on Huang's return, while Anthropic's stock dropped below its IPO price just days after its blockbuster debut, with Dario and Daniela Amodei having each sold over $280 million in shares.

stories.headline: Megaspeed, firm at center of Huang scandal, heads for US blacklist
stories.summary: Hours after Huang's reinstatement, the US government moved to blacklist Megaspeed, the chip firm previously linked to Alice Huang, which would bar it from doing business with US companies without a special license amid an ongoing national security investigation.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
stories.summary: CrowdStrike is making a record-breaking $44 billion bet on Zscaler, promising tighter security integration even as customers worry about higher prices and vendor lock-in.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to let AI agents approve code changes
stories.summary: Anthropic's new beta tool, Claude Ship, lets AI agents review, fix, and approve pull requests according to team guidelines, aiming to remove a human bottleneck as AI-generated code piles up.

stories.headline: Insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models may be uncontrollable
stories.summary: According to an Axios report cited by The Decoder, numerous employees at OpenAI and Anthropic believe their companies' unreleased frontier models can no longer be safely controlled, prompting internal debate over whether to release them.

stories.headline: Data centers are building their own natural gas power plants to dodge grid delays
stories.summary: Facing grid-connection waits that can last a decade, some data center operators are turning to dedicated natural gas power plants to meet surging AI electricity demand.

stories.headline: IBM's offer to relocate immigrant workers abroad comes with a catch
stories.summary: IBM is ending US visa sponsorship for some employees and shifting their roles overseas, a move that helps the company retain talent but imposes steep financial and personal costs on affected workers.

Tech & AI.gaps: IEEE Spectrum's feed contained only a sponsored/vendor content item with no original AI coverage found. Wired's feed items in this window were limited to shopping guides and lifestyle content with no substantive AI/tech policy stories identified.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by the collapse of the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya over fossil-fuel language, alongside fallout from the AI boom's grip on power markets (Nvidia/Jensen Huang's return rattling energy stocks) and fresh signs of energy security stress tied to the US-Iran conflict, including surging European gas prices and suspected Iranian cyberattacks on oil tankers. Trade press (Utility Dive, Latitude Media) is also tracking grid interconnection and permitting policy moves as data center demand strains utilities.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks collapse over fossil fuel language
stories.summary: Negotiations at the UN's COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey broke down after the EU and nearly 90 other governments rejected a draft text that dropped explicit commitments to transition away from fossil fuels, putting them at odds with Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iran and Qatar.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia helm lifts energy and data center stocks
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return boosted shares of energy companies tied to AI power demand, including geothermal startup Fervo, nuclear developer X-energy, and data center firm CoreWeave; Latitude Media separately reported energy firms were "whiplashed" by the Nvidia leadership drama.

stories.headline: European gas prices surge as cold snap threatens winter supplies
stories.summary: European natural gas futures jumped as much as 8.6% on forecasts for a prolonged cold spell across northwest Europe, compounding supply pressure already caused by export disruptions linked to the US-Iran war.

stories.headline: Oil prices rebound as shipping risks persist in the Middle East
stories.summary: Oil prices recovered from early losses as traders balanced ongoing threats to Middle East energy shipments against expectations of a looming global supply surplus.

stories.headline: US suspects Iran in wave of cyberattacks on oil tankers
stories.summary: US officials believe Iran may be behind a new wave of cyberattacks targeting dozens of ships carrying oil and other hazardous cargo.

stories.headline: Senate clears permitting reform bill after split among environmental groups
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports the Senate advanced a bipartisan permitting reform package, a move that divided green groups even as it's expected to speed up both clean energy and fossil fuel project buildout.

stories.headline: Mitsubishi Heavy CEO says off-grid costs will push data centers back to utilities
stories.summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries CEO Eisaku Ito argued that rising off-grid power costs will eventually drive data centers back toward utility-supplied electricity, expressing confidence in utilities' long-term expansion despite uncertainty over how much projected AI demand will materialize.

stories.headline: FERC approves MISO plan to speed up legacy interconnection studies
stories.summary: Federal regulators approved changes to the Midcontinent Independent System Operator's interconnection study process, averting delays to roughly 125 GW of generation and storage projects stuck in its queue.

Energy.gaps: Canary Media and E&E News had no stories published within the last 24-48 hours (their most recent available content was over a week old). Argus Media could not be searched due to the search limit and had no feed items provided. Reuters, FT, NYT and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items supplied for this period.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by two major political/tech shocks: the surprise investigation of Shanghai's Communist Party chief Chen Jining, and the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, which is reshaping the US-China chip-policy debate. Business and trade outlets are also tracking a new EU safeguard quota on Chinese hybrid vehicles, soft Chinese industrial data, and a wave of Chinese AI product launches, while Hong Kong outlets focus on the first anniversary of the Tai Po fire and security preparations for the Interpol General Assembly.

stories.headline: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining placed under investigation
stories.summary: Shanghai Communist Party Secretary Chen Jining, a Politburo member once tipped for further promotion, has been placed under investigation for suspected serious violations of discipline and law, becoming the first sitting Shanghai chief probed in two decades and the fourth Politburo member caught up in anti-corruption action since 2022.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang's Nvidia return threatens to deepen US rift over China chip curbs
stories.summary: Huang's return as Nvidia CEO could complicate Washington's China policy by widening the gap between a White House seeking steadier ties with Beijing and an incoming Democratic-led Congress pushing for tougher chip export controls.

stories.headline: EU imposes hybrid car import quotas on China from December 1
stories.summary: The European Commission will cap hybrid vehicle imports under provisional safeguard measures lasting up to 200 days, setting country quotas about 15% above 2025 levels, prompting China's commerce ministry to urge the EU to honor their earlier trade consensus and warn it reserves WTO dispute rights.

stories.headline: China's industrial output growth slows sharply in October
stories.summary: China's value-added industrial output grew 4.8% year-on-year in October, missing forecasts and slowing from September, as weak auto manufacturing and declining steel and cement output signaled continued property-sector drag even as electronics and equipment manufacturing stayed strong.

stories.headline: Beijing warns against politicizing Tai Po fire anniversary as Hong Kong skips official memorial
stories.summary: Ahead of the first anniversary of the deadly Tai Po fire, Beijing urged Hong Kong to stay vigilant against attempts to exploit the disaster to destabilize the city, as the Hong Kong government separately ruled out an official memorial while announcing HK$630 million in new victim grants.

stories.headline: Taiwan parties make final push ahead of 2026 local elections
stories.summary: The DPP and KMT are detailing their final campaign pushes before Taiwan's 2026 elections, with the KMT expressing confidence it can retain major northern cities and officials flagging a rising threat of election interference.

stories.headline: Zhihu discloses indirect stake in DeepSeek via investment fund
stories.summary: Chinese Q&A platform Zhihu disclosed in a voluntary announcement that it holds an indirect investment in AI firm DeepSeek through a private equity fund, underscoring continued investor interest in China's homegrown AI champions.

stories.headline: Hong Kong imposes citywide drone and traffic restrictions for Interpol General Assembly
stories.summary: Hong Kong will enforce air, sea and land restrictions including a drone ban and curbs on marine traffic ahead of hosting Interpol's annual summit next week.

China.gaps: Could not retrieve recent content from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Global Times, CGTN, Yicai Global, Focus Taiwan, or Rest of World beyond what already appeared in the provided feed; Reuters, AP, NYT and The Economist provided no China-specific feed items in the supplied materials.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Israeli/Iranian outlets is dominated by the escalating US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, alongside fallout from Israel's inconclusive coalition talks and renewed debate over a possible strike on Iran. Business desks are focused on a potential mega-merger of two major Dubai banks and strains inside Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, while Nvidia's CEO reinstatement also drew heavy regional pick-up.

stories.headline: Iran vows to use 'all available means' against US naval blockade as Hormuz tanker attacks spike
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it will use all tools to confront the reimposed US naval blockade on its oil exports, as attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz have reached their highest level since the war began, with seven vessels hit since November 16 and a Jordanian sailor still missing.

stories.headline: Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity talks stall as PM vows to topple any 'bad government'
stories.summary: Netanyahu told his Likud faction he would work to bring down any future government he deems harmful, as his unity talks with Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party dragged on for a third week without a breakthrough and Israeli military intelligence reportedly warned a strike on Iran could ignite a multi-front war.

stories.headline: Dubai Islamic Bank shares surge 11% on potential Emirates NBD merger talks
stories.summary: Dubai Islamic Bank's stock jumped after it said its board will meet this week to evaluate a strategic acquisition amid reports of preliminary talks to combine with Emirates Islamic, a deal that would rank among the UAE's biggest banking mergers.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia's $1trn Public Investment Fund faces an 'identity crisis'
stories.summary: The Economist reports that Saudi Arabia's giant sovereign wealth fund is struggling with a loss of strategic focus, with distractions going beyond the regional war.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares jump 30% as board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's board reversed its earlier decision and reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just weeks after he stepped down over revelations of affairs, including one with a suspected spy, sending the stock sharply higher.

stories.headline: Israeli strike kills UNRWA worker in Gaza as hearing-aid shortage deepens
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed a Gaza man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency, Al-Monitor reports, as Al Jazeera separately highlighted how Israeli restrictions have left Gaza facing a severe shortage of hearing-aid batteries.

stories.headline: PKK evacuates 14 more bases in northern Iraq in boost to Turkey peace deal
stories.summary: Turkish state media reported that PKK militants have withdrawn from 14 more bases in northern Iraq, marking further progress in the emerging peace process between Ankara and the Kurdish group.

stories.headline: COP31 talks end in deadlock, but analysts say shift from fossil fuels will continue
stories.summary: Climate analysts cited by The National said the collapse of COP31 negotiations will not reverse the global move away from fossil fuels, even as the summit failed to produce an agreement.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not independently verify current front-page leads for Arabian Business, AGBI, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews, Haaretz or Iran International beyond what surfaced incidentally in searches; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and BBC block search so only items from the provided feed (none for these five) could be used.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa-focused outlets are converging on DRC's critical minerals politics (a fresh cobalt export ban and a brewing Tshisekedi-Church standoff), a US-Russia geopolitical tussle over Western Sahara following Russia's UN veto, and election-season political maneuvering in Gambia. TechCabal and Bloomberg add business-and-finance angles, from telecom data demand in Benin to investor appetite for African local-currency bonds despite currency volatility.

stories.headline: DRC to reinstate cobalt export ban as prices slide
stories.summary: Mining Weekly, citing Bloomberg, reports that top cobalt producer Democratic Republic of Congo will reintroduce a ban on exports of the battery metal from the end of the month in an effort to reverse slumping prices.

stories.headline: Western Sahara emerges as a flashpoint in US-Russia rivalry
stories.summary: The Africa Report says Russia's Security Council veto on the UN's Minurso peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara signals Moscow's intent to challenge Washington's influence in the region; Africa Confidential's latest issue similarly frames the UN pullback as handing Morocco a strategic prize.

stories.headline: DRC: Tshisekedi and the Catholic Church edge toward confrontation
stories.summary: Two of Congo's most influential bishops, previously discreet amid closed-door national dialogue talks, are now openly expressing anger at President Tshisekedi, raising the prospect of a public rift.

stories.headline: Gambia's Barrow seeks a third term despite earlier pledge to step down
stories.summary: President Adama Barrow is running again in Gambia's 5 December election despite previously promising to leave office, with no term limits standing in his way.

stories.headline: Sudan's army uses El Obeid as launchpad for westward offensive
stories.summary: Reporting from the strategic city, The Africa Report details how former rebels, civilian volunteers and Islamist fighters are backing Sudanese army forces in a new push westward.

stories.headline: Senegal reinstated as 2025 AFCON champions over Morocco
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled in Senegal's favour over January's controversial Africa Cup of Nations final, reversing the result against Morocco.

stories.headline: MTN Benin outpaces its own $215m network investment plan
stories.summary: MTN Benin is being forced to accelerate spending beyond its planned $215 million as a surge in customer data traffic outstrips capacity, complicating its push to migrate users onto 5G.

stories.headline: $21 billion fund doubles down on Uganda despite shilling rout
stories.summary: A $21 billion money manager is increasing its bet on Ugandan local-currency bonds even after a currency rout wiped 8% off the shilling's value last month, signalling continued investor appetite for African local debt.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed. African Business's most recent homepage items are opinion pieces and partner/sponsored content rather than fresh news, and The Continent's most recent accessible issue is from several months ago, so no current story from either could be confirmed within the 48-hour window.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past day centers on fallout from Skydance/Paramount's consolidation of CBS News and CNN, with fresh buyout waves hitting network newsrooms, alongside Puck's ownership change under RedBird Capital. Trade outlets are also closely tracking the media/political storm around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, AI's growing footprint in publishing (shopping, music, creator deals), and press-freedom friction with the Pentagon.

stories.headline: CBS News Washington bureau buyouts deepen Skydance-era cuts
stories.summary: Status reports that senior figures in CBS News' Washington bureau have quietly accepted buyout offers as the fallout from Skydance's cost-cutting continues to widen across the network.

stories.headline: RedBird Capital finalizes acquisition of Puck
stories.summary: Puck confirmed RedBird Capital Partners has closed its investment deal valuing the company at roughly $250 million, with TPG and Standard Investments exiting and RedBird becoming lead investor while Puck says it will retain editorial independence; this is based on Puck's own announcement.

stories.headline: CNN faces its own reckoning as Skydance reshuffles networks
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers published a new piece titled "The CNN Reckoning, Redux" dated November 23, continuing his coverage of upheaval at the network under its new Skydance ownership structure.

stories.headline: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang triggers media and political firestorm
stories.summary: Mediaite extensively covered bipartisan backlash after Trump personally pushed for Nvidia's board to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang, with even MAGA-aligned figures like Laura Loomer warning the move could pose national security risks tied to an alleged Chinese espionage scandal.

stories.headline: Press Gazette declares itself 'world's first' verified human-made news outlet
stories.summary: Press Gazette announced that a new service, MadeByHumans, scans its content to verify it shows no signs of AI manipulation, positioning the outlet as a early test case for authenticity branding amid AI concerns in journalism.

stories.headline: Pentagon press restrictions continue to frustrate reporters despite Hegseth briefing
stories.summary: CJR examined how Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth held a press briefing but still limited reporters' access and information, amid ongoing tension including a lawsuit from The New York Times.

stories.headline: Disney pushes deeper into streaming without clarifying costs
stories.summary: WSJ reports Disney is expanding its streaming ambitions with more content, sports programming and a possible free tier as it tries to turn streaming into a growth engine, though the financial costs remain unclear.

stories.headline: Brands increasingly add no-AI clauses to creator contracts
stories.summary: Digiday reports that brands are writing explicit no-AI clauses into creator partnership deals, with both sides needing to clarify upfront whether AI tools can be used at any stage of content production.

Media.gaps: NYT and The Guardian had no media-industry-specific items in the provided feed (The Guardian's feed item was off-topic political satire coverage); no direct search access was used for NYT, WSJ, FT or The Guardian beyond provided feed items per instructions.
